note.question: How does competition change the precision-recall balance of targeting algorithms, especially when rival firms' consumer-level predictions are correlated?
note.overview: Two firms observe correlated algorithmic conversion predictions and simultaneously choose whom to target. Strategic overlap makes the focal symmetric Nash equilibrium mixed and changes firms' precision-recall choices relative to monopoly.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: For each consumer, firms receive possibly correlated predicted conversion probabilities from their algorithms and simultaneously choose whether to target, possibly mixing as a function of the prediction. Payoffs depend on true interest, targeting cost, and whether one or both firms target the consumer. Extensions let firms first invest in lowering correlation and jointly choose prices and targeting. Overlapping targeting lowers the return to reaching the same interested consumer and makes firms randomize.
